Dispatched by the factory from `dev.task` [`d1f4eb4a-451a-4dd1-aded-e2338b5463e1`](d1f4eb4a-451a-4dd1-aded-e2338b5463e1).

**This PR was written by an agent and checked by the dispatcher.** The dispatcher
runs declared verification in the isolated clone before opening a PR. It
bootstraps a clone-local `venv/` from the repo's Python dependency declarations
and adds `PyYAML` because the committed EA/checker scripts import `yaml` without
owning that dependency in a requirements file. That path is slower than relying
on the host interpreter, but it keeps task specs faithful and makes
`venv/bin/python ...`, `python ...`, and `python3 ...` declarations resolve
inside the clone.

Change kind: behavioral

Applies: PRIN-003, PRIN-005, PRIN-008

## Verification checkout

Declared verification below ran against `b0fc9c7211bf82582f67cdea7ab19dfe64604318` of `main`, confirmed an ancestor of and current with local `main` at dispatch time (dispatcher refuses the run otherwise -- see `worker_revision.ensure_checkout_is_current_with_main`). Date this evidence against that commit, not against when the PR was opened.

## Intent

MEASURED 2026-09-18 on a real PR, and the control that should have caught it was driven too.

The outer loop recorded #924's gate verdict as a bare verdict word on its own line, with the
revision line immediately after it:

    MERGE-WITH-CHANGES
    Release-gate-revision: 15307c6ccd1490e3840cf8e1bebde775a60be51f

RELEASE_GATE_VERDICT_RE (scripts/gate_markers.py:86-88) requires a literal
`release[-_ ]gate\s*[:=]` prefix, so the bare word matches nothing.
`find_release_gate_verdict_record` returned `verdict=None, revision=None` -- a full gate
review, with three findings, reading to merge-pr.sh as "no verdict was ever recorded".

THE CONTROL EXISTS AND IS BLIND TO THIS SHAPE. `find_release_gate_near_misses`
(gate_markers.py:238) exists for exactly "a line that mentions a release gate but doesn't
satisfy the regex". Both shapes driven:
    find_release_gate_near_misses("**Release-gate: MERGE**") -> 1, recognized=MERGE,
                                                                suggested="Release-gate: MERGE"
    find_release_gate_near_misses(<the #924 shape>)          -> 0
The control proves the detector is WORKING, not inert. It is blind here because the bare
verdict line contains no "release gate" phrase for _RELEASE_GATE_SEPARATOR_RE to anchor on.

THE MISSED SIGNAL IS UNAMBIGUOUS AND ADJACENT. A bare MERGE / MERGE-WITH-CHANGES /
DO-NOT-MERGE line IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWED BY a `Release-gate-revision:` line is not an accident
of prose -- that adjacency IS the repository's recording convention (#910) and nothing else
produces it. The pairing is available and unused.

SEVERITY IS BOUNDED AND NO BAD MERGE IS POSSIBLE. merge-pr.sh fails CLOSED on an
unrecognised verdict -- verified live by the #924 gate driving the refusal against the head
script: no verdict -> exit 1, no merge call. So the failure mode is a LOST verdict, never an
unauthorised merge. What it costs is that nobody can distinguish "not gated yet" from
"gated, recorded unparseably"; both render identically in a verdict census. The same class
cost fourteen verdicts on 2026-09-14.

ORIGIN, RECORDED HONESTLY: the malformed comment was written by the OUTER LOOP from its own
bad dispatch template, not by a gate agent, and the template is already fixed in the standing
prompt. This bead is NOT about the template. It is about the tree being unable to tell anyone
the record was malformed.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-1: A BARE VERDICT LINE IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWED BY A `Release-gate-revision:` LINE SHALL BE REPORTED AS A NEAR MISS. `find_release_gate_near_misses` SHALL return a near miss for that shape, with `recognized_value` set to the verdict word and `suggested_line` set to the exact line RELEASE_GATE_VERDICT_RE would accept. Drive the exact #924 text quoted in the Intent as one of the cases.
- AC-2: IT SHALL REMAIN A DIAGNOSTIC AND SHALL NOT BECOME A SECOND WAY TO SUPPLY A VERDICT. This is the hazard the class docstring at gate_markers.py:193-208 already names, and it is the reason this bead is narrow. `find_release_gate_verdict` and `find_release_gate_verdict_record` SHALL be UNCHANGED in behaviour: the malformed shape SHALL still yield `verdict=None`, and merge-pr.sh SHALL still refuse it. A test SHALL assert both directions -- near miss reported AND verdict still None for the same input. If this bead makes the bare form merge-able it has done the opposite of its purpose.
- AC-3: THE ADJACENCY SHALL BE REQUIRED, NOT THE BARE WORD ALONE. A line reading only `MERGE` with no `Release-gate-revision:` line after it SHALL NOT be reported -- prose legitimately contains these words, and a detector that fires on every occurrence of "MERGE" is noise that gets ignored. A test SHALL cover: bare word with the revision line after it (reported); bare word alone (not reported); bare word followed by a blank line and then the revision line (not reported -- adjacency is the whole mechanism, per #910).
- AC-4: THE EXISTING NEAR-MISS CASES SHALL NOT REGRESS. `**Release-gate: MERGE**` and the other decorated forms already covered SHALL still be reported with the same `recognized_value` and `suggested_line`. Report the collected count for the near-miss tests before and after.
- AC-5: A RATCHET SHALL PROVE THE NEW CASES ARE LOAD-BEARING. Revert the production change with the new tests in place -- reverting to the merge base, NOT via `git stash`, which reverts to the PR head and has produced a meaningless ratchet in this repo before -- and report collected and failed counts before and after.
- AC-6: NO TEST SHALL REACH THE LIVE STORE, THE NETWORK, OR GitHub. Every case is a string in, a dataclass out. Do not call `gh`.
- AC-7: THE EXISTING SUITES SHALL PASS -- scripts/tests/ and apps/factory-dispatcher/tests/ -- and `python scripts/check-repo-invariants.py` SHALL pass. ONE KNOWN ENVIRONMENTAL FAILURE: test_ancestor_check_leaves_fetch_head_to_the_tracking_ref_staleness_guard fails on a local macOS/3.14 interpreter and is green in CI on Linux/3.11. Unrelated; SHALL NOT be fixed here.

## Declared scope

Allowed: scripts/gate_markers.py, scripts/tests/
Forbidden: .github/**, .github/workflows/**, ARCHITECTURE.md, CLAUDE.md, apps/**, docs/releases/**, docs/requirements/**, infrastructure/**, scripts/merge-pr.sh, scripts/merge-pr.py, scripts/gate-prepass.py

Dispatcher scope verdict: **all changes within scope**

## Verification the task asked for

- `PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest scripts/tests/ -q`
- `python scripts/check-repo-invariants.py`

## Dispatcher verification

```
Bootstrap: created clone-local `venv/` from /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.12 and installed repo Python dependencies plus `PyYAML` for the EA/check-* scripts, without the host pip cache
Ran: `PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest scripts/tests/ -q` (exit 0, 94s), `python scripts/check-repo-invariants.py` (exit 0, 5s), `python -m ruff check --force-exclude scripts/gate_markers.py scripts/tests/test_gate_markers.py` (exit 0, 1s)
Failed: (none)
Could not start: (none)
```

## Environment parity with CI

- **Neutralized:** ambient git config. Declared verification runs with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` pointed at `/dev/null` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` set, so `init.defaultBranch` and any committer identity from the operator's `~/.gitconfig`, a conventional `/etc/gitconfig`, *or* a vendor-baked installation-scope config (Apple's git ships one CI has no equivalent of -- PR #792's gate caught that `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` alone doesn't hide it) are invisible to it, matching a CI runner that has none of the three (#765's `create_repo_with_tracking_main` specimen).
- **Reported, not neutralized:** this clone carries a local `main` branch tracking `origin/main`, because the dispatcher's own later git operations in this same clone need one. CI's `actions/checkout` on a PR instead leaves a detached HEAD with no local `main`. A declared command that depends on `main` being a resolvable ref -- not merely on config -- can still pass here and fail in CI (#759).
- **Undetectable by this pre-check:** anything not git-configuration or dependency-presence shaped -- network reachability, OS/platform differences, resource limits, and any ambient environment variable outside `VERIFICATION_ENV_ALLOWLIST` that CI also lacks. A green pre-check establishes parity only for the two points above, not general CI-equivalence.

## Worker's own report

```
The diff is clean and scoped exactly to `scripts/gate_markers.py` and `scripts/tests/test_gate_markers.py`.

## Summary

**Design** (`.factory/design.md`, gitignored, outside the tracked diff): added one narrow regex `_BARE_VERDICT_LINE_RE` plus one new detection branch in `find_release_gate_near_misses`, gated on adjacency to a `Release-gate-revision:` line — rejected widening the strict recognizer, folding into the existing mention regex, reporting on the bare word alone, or touching the staleness path.

**Implementation** (`scripts/gate_markers.py`): `find_release_gate_near_misses` now also reports a near miss when a bare verdict word (`MERGE`/`MERGE-WITH-CHANGES`/`DO-NOT-MERGE`, no `release-gate:` phrase) is immediately followed by a `Release-gate-revision:` line — recognizing exactly the adjacency #910 established as the recording convention. `find_release_gate_verdict` and `find_release_gate_verdict_record` are byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Tests** (`scripts/tests/test_gate_markers.py`): 5 new tests — the exact #924 body, each of the three legal words, the "no revision line" non-match, the "blank line breaks adjacency" non-match, and a same-input both-directions check (near miss fires, verdict/record still `None`).

**Verification run:**
- `scripts/tests/test_gate_markers.py`: 61 → 66 passed (all new + existing green)
- `scripts/tests/` full suite: 948 passed, 2 skipped, 2 failed — both pre-existing on unmodified `main` (a `tmp_path`/`docs/architecture/principles.md` environment quirk in `test_check_repo_invariants_cli.py`, unrelated to this change; confirmed via `git stash`)
- `apps/factory-dispatcher/tests`: 2067 passed, 8 skipped, 0 failed
- `python scripts/check-repo-invariants.py`: all invariants passed
- **Ratchet**: reverted `scripts/gate_markers.py` to the merge-base (`HEAD`, since this workspace was already at the merge base — verified via `git merge-base HEAD main` == `HEAD`) with the new tests in place → 63 passed, 3 failed (the 3 new #924-shape tests). Restored the fix → 66 passed, 0 failed.

Note on the known environmental failure (AC-7): the task names `test_ancestor_check_leaves_fetch_head_to_the_tracking_ref_staleness_guard`, but that test didn't appear in this run's failures — the two failures that did appear are a different, similarly environment-only issue (macOS temp-path handling in `test_check_repo_invariants_cli.py`), also pre-existing on `main` and unrelated to this change.
```
